title.raw: 卷63 王肅 宋弁 Volume 63: Wang Su, Song Bian

sentences.zh: 王肅 宋弁

translations.literal: Wang Su; Song Bian
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su; Song Bian

sentences.zh: 王肅，字恭懿，琅邪臨沂人，司馬衍丞相導之後也。

translations.literal: Wang Su, styled Gongyi, was a man of Linyi in Langye, a descendant of Chancellor Dao under Emperor Xiaowu (Sima Yan).
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su, whose courtesy name was Gongyi, came from Linyi in Langye and was a descendant of Chancellor Wang Dao, who had served under Emperor Xiaowu (Sima Yan).

sentences.zh: 父奐，蕭賾尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: His father Huan was Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat under Xiao Ze.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Huan had served Xiao Ze as Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 肅少而聰辯，涉獵經史，頗有大志。

translations.literal: Su from youth was clever and eloquent, ranged through the classics and histories, and had considerable ambition.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Su was quick-witted and articulate; he read widely in the classics and histories and harbored lofty ambitions.

sentences.zh: 仕蕭賾，歷著作郎、太子舍人、司徒主簿、祕書丞。

translations.literal: He served Xiao Ze, successively holding the posts of Gentleman of the Academy, Attendant to the Heir Apparent, Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education, and Secretary of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xiao Ze he rose through the posts of Gentleman of the Academy, Attendant to the Heir Apparent, Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education, and Secretary of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 肅自謂禮、易為長，亦未能通其大義也。

translations.literal: Su considered himself strongest in the Rites and the Changes, yet he had not mastered their larger meaning either.
translations.idiomatic: Su regarded the Rites and the Changes as his strengths, though even in those he had not fully grasped their deeper principles.

sentences.zh: 父奐及兄弟並為蕭賾所殺，肅自建業來奔，是歲，太和十七年也。

translations.literal: His father Huan and his brothers were all killed by Xiao Ze; Su came from Jiankang to defect, and that year was the seventeenth year of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huan and his brothers had all been put to death on Xiao Ze's orders. Su fled Jiankang to surrender to the north; it was the seventeenth year of the Taihe reign.

sentences.zh: 高祖幸鄴，聞肅至，虛襟待之，引見問故。

translations.literal: The Emperor Gaozu was visiting Ye; when he heard Su had arrived, he opened his heart to receive him, summoned him for an audience, and asked the reason for his coming.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu was at Ye and learned that Su had arrived, he received him with an open mind, summoned him to audience, and asked why he had come.

sentences.zh: 肅辭義敏切，辯而有禮，高祖甚哀惻之。

translations.literal: Su's words were sharp and to the point, argumentative yet courteous; the Emperor Gaozu was deeply moved with pity.
translations.idiomatic: Su spoke with keen precision—forceful in argument yet courteous in manner—and the emperor was deeply moved with compassion.

sentences.zh: 遂語及為國之道，肅陳說治亂，音韻雅暢，深會帝旨。

translations.literal: They then spoke of the way to govern the state; Su set forth order and disorder, his tones elegant and fluent, deeply matching the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Their talk turned to statecraft. Su discoursed on order and chaos in a voice elegant and fluent, striking the emperor's purpose to the core.

sentences.zh: 高祖嗟納之，促席移景，不覺坐之疲淹也。

translations.literal: The Emperor Gaozu sighed and accepted it; he drew his seat closer and the sun moved on its course, yet he did not notice how long he had been sitting.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed his approval and drew his seat nearer; the sun moved across the sky before either man noticed how long they had sat there.

sentences.zh: 因言蕭氏危滅之兆，可乘之機，勸高祖大舉。

translations.literal: He then spoke of signs that the Xiao house was near ruin and of opportunities that could be seized, urging the Emperor Gaozu to launch a great campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to describe the signs that the Xiao regime was nearing collapse and the openings that could be exploited, urging the emperor to strike on a grand scale.

sentences.zh: 於是圖南之規轉銳，器重禮遇日有加焉，親貴舊臣莫能間也。

translations.literal: Thereupon the plan to march south grew keener; esteem and courteous treatment increased day by day, and none among the emperor's kin, the nobles, or the old ministers could come between them.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the plan to march south sharpened daily. The emperor's regard and favors toward Su only grew, and neither kinsmen, nobles, nor veteran ministers could come between them.

sentences.zh: 或屏左右相對談說，至夜分不罷。

translations.literal: Sometimes they dismissed attendants and spoke face to face until deep into the night without stopping.
translations.idiomatic: At times they dismissed their attendants and talked alone together far into the night without breaking off.

sentences.zh: 肅亦盡忠輸誠，無所隱避，自謂君臣之際猶玄德之遇孔明也。

translations.literal: Su likewise gave his utmost loyalty and poured out his sincerity without concealment, considering that between ruler and minister it was like Xuande meeting Kongming.
translations.idiomatic: Su for his part gave his full loyalty and candor without reserve, believing that between them ruler and minister stood as Liu Bei had with Zhuge Liang.

sentences.zh: 尋除輔國將軍、大將軍長史，賜爵開陽伯，肅固辭伯爵，許之。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed General Who Assists the State and Chief Clerk to the Grand General; he was granted the title Marquis of Kaiyang, but Su firmly declined the marquisate and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made General Who Assists the State and Chief Clerk to the Grand General, and granted the title Marquis of Kaiyang. Su firmly declined the marquisate, and the emperor allowed it.

sentences.zh: 詔肅討蕭鸞義陽。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Su to attack Yiyang, held by Xiao Luan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Su to attack Yiyang, which was held by Xiao Luan.

sentences.zh: 聽招募壯勇以為爪牙，其募士有功，賞加常募一等；

translations.literal: He was permitted to recruit stalwart warriors as his claws and teeth; for recruited soldiers with merit, rewards were one grade higher than ordinary recruitment;
translations.idiomatic: He was authorized to recruit stalwart warriors as his fighting men. Recruits who distinguished themselves were to receive rewards one grade above the usual enlistment scale;

sentences.zh: 其從肅行者，六品已下聽先擬用，然後表聞；

translations.literal: those who followed Su on campaign, of the sixth rank and below, might be provisionally appointed first and then reported by memorial;
translations.idiomatic: followers of the sixth rank and below who accompanied Su might be provisionally appointed on the spot and reported afterward by memorial;

sentences.zh: 若投化之人，聽五品已下先即優授。

translations.literal: if they were men who had come over in submission, those of the fifth rank and below might at once receive preferential appointment.
translations.idiomatic: defectors of the fifth rank and below could receive preferential appointment immediately.

sentences.zh: 於是假肅節，行平南將軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon Su was given the credential staff and acted as General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: Su was then given the credential staff and acted in the capacity of General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 肅至義陽，頻破賊軍，降者萬餘。

translations.literal: When Su reached Yiyang, he repeatedly defeated the enemy armies, and more than ten thousand surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: At Yiyang Su repeatedly routed the enemy forces, and more than ten thousand men surrendered to him.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣散騎侍郎勞之，以功進號平南將軍，賜駿馬一匹，除持節、都督豫東豫東郢三州諸軍事、[1]本將軍、豫州刺史、揚州大中正。

translations.literal: The Emperor Gaozu sent a Gentleman of the Palace Cadet to comfort him; for his merit his title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the South, he was given one fine horse, and appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in the three provinces of Eastern Yu, Eastern Yu, and Ying,[1] with his former general's title, Inspector of Yu Province, and Chief Rectifier of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a Gentleman of the Palace Cadet to congratulate him. For his achievements Su was promoted to General Who Pacifies the South and given a fine horse. He was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in the three provinces of Eastern Yu, Eastern Yu, and Ying,[1] retaining his former general's title while also serving as Inspector of Yu Province and Chief Rectifier of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 肅善於撫接，治有聲稱。

translations.literal: Su was skilled at comforting and receiving people, and his governance won a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Su excelled at winning people over, and his administration earned a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 尋徵肅入朝，高祖手詔曰：「不見君子，中心如醉，一日三歲，我勞如何。

translations.literal: Soon Su was summoned to court; the Emperor Gaozu wrote in his own hand: 'Not seeing the gentleman, my heart is as if drunk; one day is like three years—how shall I bear my longing?
translations.idiomatic: Su was soon recalled to court. The emperor wrote in his own hand: 'Without seeing you, my heart is as though drunk; each day feels like three years—how heavy is my longing for you.

sentences.zh: 飾館華林，拂席相待，卿欲以何日發汝墳也？

translations.literal: I have adorned a lodge in the Hualin Park and swept the mat to await you—on what day do you intend to set out from your tomb at Ru?
translations.idiomatic: I have prepared a lodge in Hualin Park and swept the mat in welcome. On what day will you leave your father's tomb at Ru and come?

sentences.zh: 故復此敕。」

translations.literal: Hence this further edict.'
translations.idiomatic: Hence this further message.'

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「肅丁荼虣世，志等伍胥，自拔吳州，膺求魏縣，躬操忘禮之本，而同無數之喪，誓雪怨耻，方展申復，窮諭再期，蔬縕不改，誠季世之高風，末代之孝節也。

translations.literal: Another edict read: 'Su has met a bitter and violent age; his resolve equals that of Wu Zixu. He tore himself from Wu Province to seek a county in Wei, personally observing the root of forgetting ritual yet sharing in mourning without number, vowing to wash away hatred and shame and only now about to carry out vengeance. He has been admonished again and again that the second mourning period has ended, yet he has not changed his coarse hemp and belt—truly the lofty wind of a declining age and the filial integrity of a final generation.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict stated: 'Su has come through a bitter, violent age with a resolve equal to Wu Zixu's. He tore himself away from Wu to seek refuge in Wei. Though he has set aside the fundamentals of ritual propriety, he still observes mourning beyond all measure, vowing to avenge his wrongs and only now preparing to act. Though admonished repeatedly that the second mourning period has ended, he has not laid aside his coarse hemp and mourning belt—truly the lofty conduct of a declining age and the filial devotion of a final generation.

sentences.zh: 但聖人制禮，必均愚智；

translations.literal: Yet when the sage instituted ritual, he had to make it equal for the foolish and the wise;
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the sages established ritual, they had to make one standard for the wise and the foolish alike;

sentences.zh: 先王作則，理齊盈虛。

translations.literal: when the former kings made models, they aligned principle with fullness and emptiness.
translations.idiomatic: when the former kings set precedents, they aligned principle with what is fitting in every case.

sentences.zh: 過之者俯而就之，不及者企而行之。

translations.literal: Those who exceeded it bent down to conform; those who fell short stood on tiptoe to follow it.
translations.idiomatic: Those who went too far had to bend down to meet it; those who fell short had to stretch up to reach it.

sentences.zh: 曾參居罰，寧其哀終；

translations.literal: Zeng Shen dwelt in punishment yet found peace in bringing his grief to its end;
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Shen endured punishment yet found peace in completing his mourning;

sentences.zh: 吳員處酷，豈聞四載。

translations.literal: Wu Yuan suffered cruelty—who has heard of mourning for four years?
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zixu suffered cruel wrongs—who ever heard of mourning for four years?

sentences.zh: 夫三年者，天下之達喪，古今之所一，其雖欲過禮，朕得不制之以禮乎？

translations.literal: Three years is the universally acknowledged mourning period, the same in ancient and modern times; though he wishes to exceed ritual, how can I fail to restrain him with ritual?
translations.idiomatic: Three years is the universally acknowledged mourning period, the same in every age. Though he wishes to go beyond ritual, how can I fail to bring him within ritual bounds?

sentences.zh: 有司可依禮諭之，為裁練𧝓之制。」

translations.literal: The responsible offices may admonish him according to ritual and prescribe for him the regulations for the second year of mourning in plain white.'
translations.idiomatic: Let the responsible offices admonish him according to ritual and prescribe the regulations for the second year of mourning in plain white.'

sentences.zh: 二十年七月，高祖以久旱不雨，輟膳三旦，百僚詣闕，引在中書省。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twentieth year, because of long drought without rain the Emperor Gaozu ceased meals for three mornings; the hundred officials came to the palace gate and were led into the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twentieth year, after a prolonged drought the Emperor Gaozu abstained from meals for three mornings. The officials came to the palace and were received in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 高祖在崇虛樓，遣舍人問曰：「朕知卿等至，不獲相見，卿何為而來？」

translations.literal: The Emperor Gaozu was in the Chongxu Tower and sent a chamberlain to ask: 'I know you have come but cannot meet you—why have you come?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was in the Chongxu Tower and sent a chamberlain to ask: 'I know you have arrived but cannot receive you in audience. Why have you come?'

sentences.zh: 肅對曰：「伏承陛下輟膳已經三旦，羣臣焦怖，不敢自寧。

translations.literal: Su replied: 'I have heard humbly that Your Majesty has ceased meals for three mornings already; the officials are anxious and fearful and dare not be at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Su replied: 'We have learned that Your Majesty has abstained from meals for three mornings. The officials are consumed with anxiety and dare not rest easy.

sentences.zh: 臣聞堯水湯旱，自然之數，須聖人以濟世，不由聖以致災。

translations.literal: I have heard that the floods of Yao and the drought of Tang were part of nature's cycles; it requires a sage to rescue the age—disaster does not come because one is a sage.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the floods in Yao's time and the drought in Tang's were part of nature's cycles. It takes a sage to rescue the age—calamity does not arise because one is a sage.

sentences.zh: 是以國儲九年，以禦九年之變。

translations.literal: Therefore the state stores grain for nine years to meet nine years of change.
translations.idiomatic: That is why a state stores grain for nine years, to meet nine years of hardship.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞至於八月不雨，然後君不舉膳。

translations.literal: I have also heard that only when there is no rain until the eighth month does the ruler then cease meals.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that a ruler should abstain from meals only when rain has failed until the eighth month.

sentences.zh: 昨四郊之外已蒙滂澍，唯京城之內微為少澤。

translations.literal: Yesterday beyond the four suburbs there was already a soaking rain; only within the capital there was somewhat less moisture.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday the countryside beyond the four suburbs already received heavy rain; only within the capital the moisture was somewhat less.

sentences.zh: 蒸民未闕一餐，陛下輟膳三日，臣庶惶惶，無復情地。」

translations.literal: The common people have not yet missed a single meal, yet Your Majesty has ceased meals for three days—the officials and people are in turmoil and have no peace of mind.'
translations.idiomatic: The common people have not yet missed a single meal, yet Your Majesty has abstained for three days. Officials and subjects alike are in turmoil and can find no peace.'

sentences.zh: 高祖遣舍人答曰：「昔堯水湯旱，賴聖人以濟民，朕雖居羣黎之上，道謝前王，今日之旱，無以救恤，應待立秋，克躬自咎。

translations.literal: The Emperor Gaozu sent the chamberlain to reply: 'In former times the floods of Yao and the drought of Tang relied on sages to rescue the people. Though I stand above the multitude, my Way falls short of the former kings. For today's drought I have no means of relief and succor; I should wait until the Beginning of Autumn and examine myself in blame.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the chamberlain to reply: 'In Yao's floods and Tang's drought, the people were saved through sages. Though I stand above the multitude, my conduct falls short of the former kings. I have no means to relieve this drought and should wait until the Beginning of Autumn to examine my own faults.

sentences.zh: 但此月十日已來，炎熱焦酷，人物同悴，而連雲數日，高風蕭條，雖不食數朝，猶自無感，朕誠心未至之所致也。」

translations.literal: Yet from the tenth of this month the heat has been scorching and fierce, men and things alike withered, while for days on end clouds have massed and high winds blown bleak—though I have not eaten for several mornings, still there is no response; it is because my sincere heart has not yet reached the mark.'
translations.idiomatic: Yet since the tenth of this month the heat has been fierce and all creation withers, while clouds have massed for days and high winds blow bleak. Though I have abstained for several mornings, heaven still does not respond—it is because my sincerity has not yet been sufficient.'

sentences.zh: 肅曰：「臣聞聖人與凡同者五常，異者神明。

translations.literal: Su said: 'I have heard that what sages share with ordinary men is the five constant virtues; what sets them apart is their divine clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Su said: 'I have heard that what sages share with ordinary men are the five constant virtues; what sets them apart is their divine clarity.

sentences.zh: 昔姑射之神，不食五穀，臣常謂矯。

translations.literal: In old times the spirit of Mount Guye did not eat the five grains—I always considered that pretense.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit of Mount Guye in antiquity did not eat grain—I always took that for pretense.

sentences.zh: 今見陛下，始知其驗。

translations.literal: Now that I see Your Majesty, I begin to know it is verified.
translations.idiomatic: Now that I see Your Majesty, I know it can be true.

sentences.zh: 且陛下自輟膳以來，若天全無應，臣亦謂上天無知，陛下無感。

translations.literal: Moreover, since Your Majesty ceased meals, if Heaven had given no response at all, I too would say that Heaven was without knowledge and Your Majesty without efficacy.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, since Your Majesty began abstaining, if heaven had given no response at all, I too would say heaven was unaware and Your Majesty's sincerity had not moved it.

sentences.zh: 一昨之前，外有滂澤，此有密雲，臣即謂天有知，陛下有感矣。」

translations.literal: Before yesterday, outside there was a soaking rain and here dense clouds—I would then say Heaven has knowledge and Your Majesty has efficacy.'
translations.idiomatic: Before yesterday there was heavy rain outside and dense clouds here—I would say heaven has taken notice and Your Majesty's sincerity has moved it.'

sentences.zh: 高祖遣舍人答曰：「昨內外貴賤咸云四郊有雨，朕恐此輩皆勉勸之辭，三覆之慎，必欲使信而有徵。

translations.literal: The Emperor Gaozu sent the chamberlain to reply: 'Yesterday nobles and commoners within and without all said there was rain in the four suburbs; I fear these were all words of urging and encouragement. With the caution of thrice reviewing, I must make belief have proof and evidence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the chamberlain to reply: 'Yesterday everyone within and without the court said the four suburbs had rain. I fear these were words of encouragement. I must be thrice cautious and require proof before I believe.

sentences.zh: 比當遣人往行，若果雨也，便命大官欣然進膳。

translations.literal: Shortly I shall send men to go and verify; if there is truly rain, I shall order the Grand Provisioner gladly to present meals.
translations.idiomatic: I shall soon send men to verify. If rain has truly fallen, I shall order the Grand Provisioner to serve meals with gladness.

sentences.zh: 豈可以近郊之內而慷慨要天乎？

translations.literal: How can one within the near suburbs make passionate demands of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: How can one within the near suburbs make passionate demands of heaven?

sentences.zh: 若其無也，朕之無感，安用朕身以擾民庶！

translations.literal: If there is none, then my lack of efficacy—of what use is my person to trouble the people!
translations.idiomatic: If there is none, then my sincerity has not moved heaven—of what use is my person to trouble the people!

sentences.zh: 朕志確然，死而後已。」

translations.literal: My resolve is firm and will not cease until death.'
translations.idiomatic: My resolve is firm and will not cease until death.'

sentences.zh: 是夜澍雨大降。

translations.literal: That night a great timely rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: That night a soaking rain fell in abundance.

sentences.zh: 以破蕭鸞將裴叔業功，進號鎮南將軍，加都督豫、南兗、東荊、東豫四州諸軍事，封汝陽縣開國子，食邑三百戶，持節、中正、刺史如故。

translations.literal: For the merit of defeating Xiao Luan's general Pei Shuye, his title was advanced to General Who Guards the South; he was made Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in the four provinces of Yu, Southern Yanzhou, Eastern Jing, and Eastern Yu; enfeoffed as Viscount of Ruyang with an estate of three hundred households; Bearer of the Staff, Rectifier, and Inspector as before.
translations.idiomatic: For defeating Xiao Luan's general Pei Shuye, Su was promoted to General Who Guards the South and made Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Yu, Southern Yanzhou, Eastern Jing, and Eastern Yu. He was enfeoffed as Viscount of Ruyang with an estate of three hundred households, retaining his credential staff, rectifier's post, and inspector's title.

sentences.zh: 肅頻表固讓，不許，詔加鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: Su repeatedly memorialized firmly declining; this was not granted, and an edict added one set of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: Su repeatedly memorialized to decline the honors, but the emperor would not allow it and added a set of martial music to his entourage.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，既平漢陽，詔肅曰：「夫知己貴義，君臣務恩，不能矜災卹禍，恩義焉措？

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, after Hanyang had been pacified, an edict to Su read: 'One who knows a friend values righteousness; ruler and minister must attend to grace. If one cannot show pity in disaster and relieve suffering, where is grace and righteousness to be placed?
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, after Hanyang was pacified, the emperor wrote to Su: 'A true friend values righteousness; ruler and minister must honor mutual obligation. If one cannot show pity in disaster and relieve suffering, where can grace and righteousness remain?

sentences.zh: 卿情同伍員，懷酷歸朕，然未能翦一讎人，馘彼凶帥，何嘗不興言憤歎，羨吳閭而長息。

translations.literal: Your feeling is like Wu Yuan's; you bore cruelty and came to me, yet you have not been able to cut down a single enemy or take the head of that vicious commander—how often have I not spoken in anger and sighing, envying King Helü of Wu and drawing long breaths.
translations.idiomatic: Your feelings match Wu Zixu's; you suffered cruel wrongs and came to me, yet you have not been able to cut down a single foe or take that vicious commander's head. How often have I not spoken in anger and sighing, envying King Helü of Wu and drawing long breaths.

sentences.zh: 比獲蕭鸞輔國將軍黃瑤起，乃知是卿怨也。

translations.literal: Recently we captured Xiao Luan's General Who Assists the State Huang Yaoqi—now I know this is your enemy.
translations.idiomatic: We have recently captured Xiao Luan's General Who Assists the State Huang Yaoqi—now I know he is the man you seek.

sentences.zh: 尋當相付，微望紓泄，使吾見卿之日，差得緩懷。」

translations.literal: Shortly he shall be handed over to you; I faintly hope for some easing of your grief, so that on the day I see you again my heart may be somewhat relieved.'
translations.idiomatic: He shall soon be handed over to you. I hope this may ease your grief somewhat, so that when I see you again my heart may be a little lighter.'

sentences.zh: 初，賾之收肅父奐也，司馬黃瑤起攻奐殺之，故詔云然。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ze arrested Su's father Huan, the Major Huang Yaoqi attacked Huan and killed him—hence the edict spoke thus.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Xiao Ze arrested Su's father Huan, the Major Huang Yaoqi had attacked and killed him—hence the edict spoke as it did.

sentences.zh: 高祖之伐淮北，令肅討義陽，未克，而蕭鸞遣將裴叔業寇渦陽。

translations.literal: When the Emperor Gaozu campaigned against north of the Huai, he ordered Su to attack Yiyang; it was not taken, while Xiao Luan sent the general Pei Shuye to raid Woyang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Emperor Gaozu's campaign north of the Huai, Su was ordered to attack Yiyang but had not taken it when Xiao Luan sent General Pei Shuye to raid Woyang.

sentences.zh: 劉藻等救之，為叔業所敗。

translations.literal: Liu Zao and others went to rescue it and were defeated by Shuye.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zao and others went to relieve the city but were defeated by Pei Shuye.

sentences.zh: 肅表求更遣軍援渦陽。

translations.literal: Su memorialized requesting that another army be sent to aid Woyang.
translations.idiomatic: Su memorialized asking that another army be sent to relieve Woyang.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「得表，覽之憮然，觀卿意非專在水，當是以藻等銳兵新敗於前，事往勢難故也。

translations.literal: An edict read: 'I have received your memorial and read it with distress. I see your intent is not solely on the river—it must be because Zao and others' crack troops were newly defeated before, the matter is past and the situation difficult.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated: 'I have received your memorial and read it with distress. I see your concern is not solely for the river—it must be because Liu Zao and the others' crack troops were just defeated, the situation has turned difficult.

sentences.zh: 朕若分兵，遣之非多，會無所制，多遣則禁旅難闕。

translations.literal: If I divide the army and send them, if not many they will be unable to control the situation; if I send many, the capital guard will be hard pressed.
translations.idiomatic: If I divide forces and send too few, they will be unable to control the situation; if I send too many, the capital guard will be dangerously depleted.

sentences.zh: 今日之計，唯當作必克之舉，不可為狐疑之師，徒失南兗也。

translations.literal: Today's plan must be to make a strike certain to succeed; one must not make an army of hesitation and vainly lose Southern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Today's plan must be a strike certain to succeed. Do not lead a hesitant force and vainly lose Southern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 卿便息意停彼，以圖義陽之寇。

translations.literal: You should set your mind at rest and halt there, to plan against the enemy at Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Set your mind at ease and hold your position there to deal with the enemy at Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 宜止則止，還取義陽；

translations.literal: If you should halt, then halt and return to take Yiyang;
translations.idiomatic: If you should hold, then hold and return to take Yiyang;

sentences.zh: 宜下則下，鎮軍淮北。

translations.literal: if you should advance, then advance and garrison the army north of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: if you should advance, then advance and garrison your forces north of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 深量二途，勿致重爽。

translations.literal: Weigh these two courses deeply and do not bring about a double failure.
translations.idiomatic: Weigh both courses carefully and do not bring about a double failure.

sentences.zh: 若孟表糧盡，軍不及至，致失渦陽，卿之過也。」

translations.literal: If Meng Biao's grain is exhausted and the army does not arrive in time, causing the loss of Woyang, it will be your fault.'
translations.idiomatic: If Meng Biao's supplies run out and your army does not arrive in time, causing Woyang to be lost, the fault will be yours.'

sentences.zh: 肅乃解義陽之圍，以赴渦陽，叔業乃引師而退。

translations.literal: Su thereupon lifted the siege of Yiyang and went to Woyang; Shuye then withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: Su thereupon lifted the siege of Yiyang and marched to Woyang, whereupon Pei Shuye withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 肅坐劉藻等敗，黜為平南將軍，中正、刺史如故。

translations.literal: Su was punished for Liu Zao and others' defeat and demoted to General Who Pacifies the South; Rectifier and Inspector as before.
translations.idiomatic: Su was demoted to General Who Pacifies the South on account of Liu Zao's defeat, but retained his posts as Rectifier and Inspector.

sentences.zh: 高祖崩，遺詔以肅為尚書令，與咸陽王禧等同為宰輔，徵肅會駕魯陽。

translations.literal: The Emperor Gaozu died; his final edict appointed Su as Director of the Imperial Secretariat, with the Prince of Xianyang Xi and others as chief ministers, and summoned Su to join the imperial procession at Luyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor Gaozu died, his final edict appointed Su Director of the Imperial Secretariat and made him a chief minister alongside the Prince of Xianyang Xi and others. Su was summoned to join the imperial procession at Luyang.

sentences.zh: 肅至，遂與禧等參同謀謨。

translations.literal: When Su arrived, he then joined Xi and the others in deliberating on policy.
translations.idiomatic: When Su arrived, he joined Xi and the others in deliberating on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 自魯陽至於京洛，行途喪紀，委肅參量，憂勤經綜，有過舊戚。

translations.literal: From Luyang to Luoyang, the mourning regulations along the route were entrusted to Su to assess; his anxious diligence in managing affairs surpassed the old kinsmen.
translations.idiomatic: From Luyang to Luoyang, the mourning arrangements along the route were entrusted to Su for oversight. His anxious diligence in managing affairs surpassed even the emperor's kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 禧兄弟並敬而昵之，上下稱為和輯。

translations.literal: Xi and his brothers all respected and drew close to him; above and below called it harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Xi and his brothers all respected and drew close to him; court and camp alike praised their harmony.

sentences.zh: 唯任城王澄以其起自羇遠，一旦在己之上，以為憾焉。

translations.literal: Only the Prince of Rencheng Cheng, because Su had risen from distant bondservant origins and suddenly stood above him, harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Prince of Rencheng Cheng resented him, for Su had risen from distant, subject origins and now stood suddenly above him.

sentences.zh: 每謂人曰：「朝廷以王肅加我上尚可，從叔廣陽，宗室尊宿，[2]歷任內外，云何一朝令肅居其右也？」

translations.literal: He often told others: 'For the court to place Wang Su above me is still tolerable, but my father's younger brother the Prince of Guangyang is a senior of the imperial clan,[2] who has served within and without—how can they in a single morning place Su to his right?'
translations.idiomatic: He often said: 'For the court to place Wang Su above me is still tolerable. But my father's younger brother the Prince of Guangyang is a senior member of the imperial clan,[2] who has served in posts within and without the capital—how can they place Su to his right in a single morning?'

sentences.zh: 肅聞其言，恒降而避之。

translations.literal: When Su heard these words, he always lowered himself and avoided him.
translations.idiomatic: When Su heard this, he always deferred to him and kept his distance.

sentences.zh: 尋為澄所奏劾，稱肅謀叛，言尋申釋。

translations.literal: Soon he was impeached by Cheng, who charged that Su plotted rebellion; the charge was soon clarified and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Cheng impeached him, charging Su with plotting rebellion; the charge was soon clarified and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 詔肅尚陳留長公主，本劉昶子婦彭城公主也，賜錢二十萬、帛三千匹。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Su to marry the Elder Princess of Chenliu, who had been the daughter-in-law of Liu Chang, the Princess of Pengcheng; he was granted two hundred thousand cash and three thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Su to marry the Elder Princess of Chenliu, formerly the Princess of Pengcheng and daughter-in-law of Liu Chang. He was granted two hundred thousand cash and three thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 肅奏：「考以顯能，陟由績著，昇明退闇，於是乎在。

translations.literal: Su memorialized: 'Examination is to display ability; promotion follows outstanding achievement; raising the enlightened and removing the obscure—herein lies the principle.
translations.idiomatic: Su memorialized: 'Examinations reveal ability; promotion follows outstanding achievement. Raising the capable and removing the incompetent—that is the principle.

sentences.zh: 自百僚曠察，四稔于茲，請依舊式考檢能否。」

translations.literal: Since the hundred officials have gone without inspection for four years now, I request that examinations be conducted according to the old form to test ability.'
translations.idiomatic: The officials have gone without inspection for four years now. I request that examinations be conducted according to the established form to test their competence.'

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 裴叔業以壽春內附，拜肅使持節、都督江西諸軍事、車騎將軍，與驃騎大將軍、彭城王勰率步騎十萬以赴之。

translations.literal: When Pei Shuye submitted Shouchun to the north, Su was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs west of the river, and General of the Chariots and Cavalry, and with the General of Agile Cavalry, the Prince of Pengcheng Xie, led one hundred thousand infantry and cavalry to go to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Shuye surrendered Shouchun to the north, Su was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs west of the river, and General of the Chariots and Cavalry. He joined the General of Agile Cavalry, the Prince of Pengcheng Xie, in leading one hundred thousand infantry and cavalry to the scene.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶卷豫州刺史蕭懿率眾三萬屯於小峴，交州刺史李叔獻屯合肥，將圖壽春。

translations.literal: Xiao Baojuan's Inspector of Yu Province Xiao Yi led thirty thousand men and encamped at Xiaoxian; the Inspector of Jiaozhou Li Shuxian encamped at Hefei, intending to take Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Baojuan's Inspector of Yu Province Xiao Yi led thirty thousand men to encamp at Xiaoxian, while the Inspector of Jiaozhou Li Shuxian encamped at Hefei, both intending to retake Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 懿遣將胡松、李居士等領眾萬餘屯據死虎。

translations.literal: Yi sent the generals Hu Song, Li Jushi, and others to lead more than ten thousand men to encamp and hold Sihu.
translations.idiomatic: Yi sent Generals Hu Song, Li Jushi, and others with more than ten thousand men to hold the fortress of Sihu.

sentences.zh: 肅進師討擊，大破之，擒其將橋珉等，斬首數千。

translations.literal: Su advanced his army to attack and inflicted a great defeat, capturing their generals Qiao Min and others and taking several thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Su advanced to attack and routed them utterly, capturing Generals Qiao Min and others and taking several thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 進討合肥，生擒叔獻，蕭懿棄小峴南走。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack Hefei, captured Shuxian alive, and Xiao Yi abandoned Xiaoxian and fled south.
translations.idiomatic: He then advanced on Hefei and took Li Shuxian alive. Xiao Yi abandoned Xiaoxian and fled south.

sentences.zh: 肅還京師，世宗臨東堂引見勞之，又問：「江左有何息耗？」

translations.literal: When Su returned to the capital, the Emperor Shizong came to the Eastern Hall to receive him in audience and comfort him, and also asked: 'What news is there from the lands south of the Yangtze?'
translations.idiomatic: When Su returned to the capital, Emperor Shizong received him in audience at the Eastern Hall and congratulated him, then asked: 'What news is there from south of the Yangtze?'

sentences.zh: 肅曰：「如聞崔慧景已死。

translations.literal: Su said: 'As I have heard, Cui Huijing is already dead.
translations.idiomatic: Su replied: 'As I have heard, Cui Huijing is already dead.

sentences.zh: 寶卷所仗，非邪即佞。

translations.literal: Those on whom Baojuan relies are either wicked or sycophantic.
translations.idiomatic: Those Baojuan relies on are either wicked or sycophantic.

sentences.zh: 天殆以此資陛下，廓定之期，勢將不久。」

translations.literal: Heaven is perhaps thereby furnishing Your Majesty; the time for pacification and settlement will not be long.'
translations.idiomatic: Heaven may be furnishing Your Majesty with the means; the time for pacification cannot be far off.'

sentences.zh: 以肅淮南累捷，賞帛四千七百五十匹，進位開府儀同三司，封昌國縣開國侯，食邑八百戶，餘如故。

translations.literal: For Su's repeated victories in Huainan, he was rewarded with four thousand seven hundred fifty bolts of silk, advanced to the rank of Bearer of the Staff with the Ceremonies of the Three Dukes, enfeoffed as Marquis of Changguo with an estate of eight hundred households; the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: For Su's repeated victories in Huainan, he was rewarded with four thousand seven hundred fifty bolts of silk, promoted to Bearer of the Staff with the Ceremonies of the Three Dukes, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Changguo with an estate of eight hundred households; his other titles remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 尋以肅為散騎常侍、都督淮南諸軍事、揚州刺史、持節，餘官如故。

translations.literal: Soon Su was made Attendant at the Palace Cadet, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Huainan, Inspector of Yang Province, and Bearer of the Staff; his other offices as before.
translations.idiomatic: Su was soon made Attendant at the Palace Cadet, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Huainan, Inspector of Yang Province, and Bearer of the Staff, while his other offices remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 肅頻在邊，悉心撫接，遠近歸懷，附者若市，以誠綏納，咸得其心。

translations.literal: Su was often on the frontier, devoting his heart to comforting and receiving people; near and far turned to him in allegiance, and those who attached themselves were like a market crowd; by sincerity he soothed and accepted them, and all won their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Su was often on the frontier and devoted himself to winning people over. Near and far alike turned to him in allegiance, and those who came to join him were as numerous as a market crowd. Through sincere kindness he won them all.

sentences.zh: 清身好施，簡絕聲色，終始廉約，家無餘財。

translations.literal: He kept his person pure and delighted in giving; he set aside music and women; from first to last he was frugal, and his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He lived plainly and gave generously, shunning music and women. Throughout his life he was frugal, and his household left no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 然性微輕佻，頗以功名自許，護疵稱伐，少所推下，高祖每以此為言。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was slightly frivolous; he rather prided himself on fame and achievement, shielded his flaws and boasted of his merits, and seldom deferred to those below him—the Emperor Gaozu often spoke of this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was somewhat frivolous by nature, took pride in fame and achievement, glossed over his faults while trumpeting his merits, and seldom deferred to others. The Emperor Gaozu often remarked on this.

sentences.zh: 景明二年薨於壽春，年三十八。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingming he died at Shouchun, aged thirty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Jingming reign he died at Shouchun, at the age of thirty-eight.

sentences.zh: 世宗為舉哀，詔曰：「肅奄至不救，痛惋兼懷，可遣中書侍郎賈思伯兼通直散騎常侍撫慰厥孤，給東園祕器、朝服一襲、錢三十萬、帛一千匹、布五百匹、蠟三百斤，并問其卜遷遠近，專遣侍御史一人監護喪事，務令優厚。」

translations.literal: The Emperor Shizong held mourning for him; an edict read: 'Su has suddenly arrived beyond rescue; grief and regret fill my heart together. Let Palace Attendant Jia Sibo, also acting as Direct Attendant at the Palace Cadet, go to comfort his orphans. Grant the secret funerary vessels of the Eastern Garden, one set of court robes, three hundred thousand cash, one thousand bolts of silk, five hundred bolts of cloth, and three hundred jin of wax. Also inquire about the distance for divining the burial site, and specially send one Attending Censor to oversee the funeral affairs, ensuring that all be generous.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong ordered mourning rites. An edict stated: 'Su's sudden death fills me with grief and regret. Send Palace Attendant Jia Sibo, also acting as Direct Attendant at the Palace Cadet, to comfort his orphans. Grant the secret funerary vessels of the Eastern Garden, one set of court robes, three hundred thousand cash, one thousand bolts of silk, five hundred bolts of cloth, and three hundred jin of wax. Inquire about the distance for choosing a burial site, and send a dedicated Attending Censor to oversee the funeral, ensuring that all arrangements be generous.'

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「死生動靜，卑高有域，勝達所居，存亡崇顯。

translations.literal: Another edict read: 'Life and death, movement and stillness, low and high each have their domain; where the eminent dwell, survival and extinction are honored and displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict stated: 'Life and death, movement and stillness, high and low each have their proper domain. Where the eminent rest, survival and extinction alike are honored and displayed.

sentences.zh: 故杜預之歿，窆於首陽；

translations.literal: Thus when Du Yu died, he was buried at Shouyang;
translations.idiomatic: When Du Yu died, he was buried at Shouyang;

sentences.zh: 司空李沖，覆舟是託。

translations.literal: the Minister of Works Li Chong was entrusted to the capsized boat.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Li Chong was laid to rest beside the capsized boat.

sentences.zh: 顧瞻斯所，誠亦二代之九原也。

translations.literal: Looking upon this place, it is truly the Jiuyuan of two dynasties as well.
translations.idiomatic: Gazing upon this place, it is truly a burial ground worthy of two dynasties.

sentences.zh: 故揚州刺史肅誠義結於二世，英惠符於李杜，平生本意，願終京陵，既有宿心，宜遂先志。

translations.literal: The former Inspector of Yang Province Su bound his sincere righteousness to two emperors; his brilliance and kindness matched Li and Du; his lifelong intent was to end at the capital tombs—since he already had this longstanding wish, his former purpose should be fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: The former Inspector of Yang Province Su bound his loyalty to two emperors, and his brilliance and kindness matched those of Li Chong and Du Yu. His lifelong wish was to be buried at the capital tombs. Since this was his longstanding desire, his former purpose should be fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 其令葬於沖、預兩墳之間，使之神遊相得也。」

translations.literal: Let him be buried between the two tombs of Chong and Yu, so that their spirits may roam and find one another.'
translations.idiomatic: Let him be buried between the tombs of Li Chong and Du Yu, so that their spirits may keep company in the afterlife.'

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、司空公，本官如故。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Palace Attendant and Minister of Works; his former offices as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Palace Attendant and Minister of Works, while his former titles remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 有司奏以肅忠心大度，宜諡匡公，詔諡宣簡。

translations.literal: The responsible offices memorialized that Su's loyal heart and great magnanimity suited the posthumous title Lord Kuang; an edict gave the posthumous title Xuanjian.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices recommended the posthumous title Lord Kuang for Su's loyal heart and great magnanimity, but an edict granted the posthumous title Xuanjian.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，詔為肅建碑銘。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Suzong reign, an edict ordered that a stele inscription be erected for Su.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Suzong reign, an edict ordered a memorial stele erected for Su.

sentences.zh: 子紹襲。

translations.literal: His son Shao inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shao inherited his titles.

sentences.zh: 紹，字三歸。

translations.literal: Shao, styled Sangui.
translations.idiomatic: Shao, whose courtesy name was Sangui.

sentences.zh: 歷官太子洗馬、員外常侍、中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Groom of the Heir Apparent, Acting Regular Attendant, and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Groom of the Heir Apparent, Acting Regular Attendant, and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈輔國將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously granted General Who Assists the State and Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made General Who Assists the State and Inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 子遷，襲。

translations.literal: His son Qian inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qian inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 武定中，通直常侍。

translations.literal: During Wuding, Direct Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wuding reign he served as Direct Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵隨例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, his noble rank was reduced according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, his noble rank was reduced according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 紹弟理，孝靜初，始得還朝。

translations.literal: Shao's younger brother Li, at the beginning of Xiaojing, was at last able to return to court.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's younger brother Li was at last able to return to court early in the Xiaojing reign.

sentences.zh: 武定末，著作佐郎。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding, Assistant Gentleman of the Academy.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Wuding reign he served as Assistant Gentleman of the Academy.

sentences.zh: 紹，肅前妻謝生也，肅臨薨，謝始攜二女及紹至壽春。

translations.literal: Shao was the son of Su's former wife, Lady Xie; when Su was near death, Xie at last brought her two daughters and Shao to Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was the son of Su's former wife, Lady Xie. When Su was dying, Lady Xie at last brought her two daughters and Shao to Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 世宗納其女為夫人，肅宗又納紹女為嬪。

translations.literal: The Emperor Shizong took his daughter as Lady; the Emperor Suzong also took Shao's daughter as Imperial Concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong took his daughter as a consort, and Emperor Suzong later took Shao's daughter as an imperial concubine.

sentences.zh: 肅弟秉，字文政。

translations.literal: Su's younger brother Bing, styled Wenzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Su's younger brother Bing, whose courtesy name was Wenzheng.

sentences.zh: 涉獵書史，微有兄風。

translations.literal: He ranged through books and histories and had a slight trace of his elder brother's manner.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in books and histories and showed something of his elder brother's manner.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，攜兄子誦、翊、衍等入國，拜中書郎，遷司徒諮議，出為輔國將軍、幽州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shizong, he brought his elder brother's sons Song, Yi, Yan, and others into the state; he was appointed Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat, promoted to Adviser to the Minister of Education, and sent out as General Who Assists the State and Inspector of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shizong reign he brought his elder brother's sons Song, Yi, Yan, and others into Wei territory. He was appointed Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat, then Adviser to the Minister of Education, and later sent out as General Who Assists the State and Inspector of You Province.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈征虜將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously granted General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 誦，字國章，肅長兄融之子。

translations.literal: Song, styled Guozhang, was the son of Su's elder brother Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Song, whose courtesy name was Guozhang, was the son of Su's elder brother Rong.

sentences.zh: 學涉有文才，神氣清儁，風流甚美。

translations.literal: He studied broadly and had literary talent; his spirit was clear and handsome, and his bearing exceedingly fine.
translations.idiomatic: He was learned and gifted in letters, with a clear and handsome presence and an exceptionally refined bearing.

sentences.zh: 自員外郎、司徒主簿，轉司徒屬、司空諮議、通直常侍、汝南王友。

translations.literal: From Gentleman of the Palace, Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education, he was transferred to Attendant of the Minister of Education, Adviser to the Minister of Works, Direct Regular Attendant, and Companion to the Prince of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from Gentleman of the Palace and Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education to Attendant of the Minister of Education, Adviser to the Minister of Works, Direct Regular Attendant, and Companion to the Prince of Runan.

sentences.zh: 遷司徒諮議，加前軍、散騎常侍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Adviser to the Minister of Education, with additional titles of Vanguard General, Attendant at the Palace Cadet, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Adviser to the Minister of Education, with additional titles of Vanguard General, Attendant at the Palace Cadet, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 出為左將軍、幽州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as General of the Left and Inspector of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General of the Left and Inspector of You Province.

sentences.zh: 未幾，徵為長兼祕書監，徙給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned as Senior Acting Director of the Palace Library, then transferred to Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled as Senior Acting Director of the Palace Library, then transferred to Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 肅宗崩，靈太后之立幼主也，於時大赦，誦宣讀詔書，音制抑揚，風神疎秀，百僚傾屬，莫不歎美。

translations.literal: When Suzong died and Empress Dowager Ling established the young ruler, there was at the time a great amnesty; Song read the edict aloud, his tones rising and falling, his bearing open and refined; the hundred officials turned to him, and none failed to sigh in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong died and Empress Dowager Ling installed the young emperor, a general amnesty was proclaimed. Song read the edict aloud with cadences rising and falling, his bearing open and refined. The officials all turned to him in admiration.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，於河陰遇害，年三十七。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaozhuang, he met with violence at Heyin, aged thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiaozhuang reign he was killed at Heyin, at the age of thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: [3]贈驃騎大將軍、尚書左僕射、司空公、徐州刺史，諡曰文宣。

translations.literal: [3] Posthumously granted General of Agile Cavalry, Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Minister of Works, and Inspector of Xuzhou; posthumous title Wenhuan.
translations.idiomatic: [3] He was posthumously made General of Agile Cavalry, Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Minister of Works, and Inspector of Xuzhou, with the posthumous title Wenhuan.

sentences.zh: 子孝康，武定中，尚書郎中。

translations.literal: His son Xiaokang, during Wuding, Gentleman of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaokang served as Gentleman of the Imperial Secretariat during the Wuding reign.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 孝康弟儁康，性清雅，頗有文才。

translations.literal: Xiaokang's younger brother Junkang was refined and elegant by nature and had considerable literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokang's younger brother Junkang was refined and elegant by nature and showed considerable literary talent.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄王中外府祭酒。

translations.literal: Libationer of the Central and Outer Office of the Prince of Wenxiang of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Libationer of the Central and Outer Office under the Prince of Wenxiang of Qi.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈征虜將軍、太府少卿。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously granted General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Vice Director of the Grand Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Vice Director of the Grand Treasury.

sentences.zh: 誦弟衍，字文舒。

translations.literal: Song's younger brother Yan, styled Wenshu.
translations.idiomatic: Song's younger brother Yan, whose courtesy name was Wenshu.

sentences.zh: 名行器藝亞於誦。

translations.literal: His reputation, conduct, talent, and skill were second to Song's.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation, conduct, and abilities were second only to Song's.

sentences.zh: 自著作佐郎，稍遷尚書郎、員外常侍、司空諮議、光祿大夫、廷尉、揚州大中正、度支尚書，仍轉七兵，徙太常卿。

translations.literal: From Assistant Gentleman of the Academy he was gradually promoted to Gentleman of the Imperial Secretariat, Acting Regular Attendant, Adviser to the Minister of Works, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Minister of Justice, Chief Rectifier of Yang Province, Director of Revenue, then transferred to the Seven Troops, and moved to Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as Assistant Gentleman of the Academy, he rose through Gentleman of the Imperial Secretariat, Acting Regular Attendant, Adviser to the Minister of Works, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Minister of Justice, Chief Rectifier of Yang Province, and Director of Revenue, then transferred to the Seven Troops and became Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 出為散騎常侍、征東將軍、西兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Attendant at the Palace Cadet, General Who Conquers the East, and Inspector of Western Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Attendant at the Palace Cadet, General Who Conquers the East, and Inspector of Western Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 衍屆治未幾，屬尒朱仲遠稱兵內向，州既路衝，為其攻逼。

translations.literal: Yan had been in office only a short time when Erzhu Zhongyuan raised troops and marched inward; the province being on the main route, he was attacked and pressed by him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had been in office only a short time when Erzhu Zhongyuan raised troops and marched inward. The province lay on the main route and came under his attack.

sentences.zh: 衍不能守，為仲遠所擒，以其名望不害也，令其騎牛從軍，久乃見釋。

translations.literal: Yan could not hold it and was captured by Zhongyuan; because of his reputation he was not harmed, but was made to ride an ox with the army; only after a long time was he released.
translations.idiomatic: Yan could not hold the province and was captured by Zhongyuan. Because of his reputation he was not harmed, but was made to ride an ox with the army. Only after a long time was he released.

sentences.zh: 還洛，除車騎將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Returning to Luoyang, he was appointed General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to Luoyang he was made General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 孝靜初，轉侍中，將軍如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojing, he was transferred to Palace Attendant; his general's title as before.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiaojing reign he was made Palace Attendant while retaining his general's title.

sentences.zh: 天平三年卒，年五十二。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianping he died, aged fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Tianping reign he died, at the age of fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 敕給東園祕器、賵物三百段，贈使持節、都督青徐兗三州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、尚書令、司徒公、徐州刺史，諡曰文獻。

translations.literal: An edict granted the secret funerary vessels of the Eastern Garden and three hundred sections of funeral goods; posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in the three provinces of Qing, Xu, and Yan, General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Minister of Education, and Inspector of Xuzhou; posthumous title Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted the secret funerary vessels of the Eastern Garden and three hundred sections of funeral goods. He was posthumously made Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Qing, Xu, and Yan provinces, General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Minister of Education, and Inspector of Xuzhou, with the posthumous title Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 衍篤於交舊，有故人竺虩，於西兗為仲遠所害，其妻子飢寒，衍置之於家，累年贍恤，世人稱其敦厚。

translations.literal: Yan was devoted to old friends; he had an old acquaintance Zhu Xi who was killed by Zhongyuan in Western Yanzhou; his wife and children were hungry and cold; Yan took them into his household and for years provided support; the world praised his generosity.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was devoted to old friends. An acquaintance named Zhu Xi had been killed by Zhongyuan in Western Yanzhou, leaving his wife and children hungry and cold. Yan took them into his household and supported them for years, and the world praised his generosity.

sentences.zh: 翊，字士遊，肅次兄琛子也。

translations.literal: Yi, styled Shiyou, was the son of Su's second elder brother Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, whose courtesy name was Shiyou, was the son of Su's second elder brother Chen.

sentences.zh: 風神秀立，好學有文才。

translations.literal: His bearing was outstanding and erect; he loved learning and had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: His bearing was outstanding; he loved learning and had literary talent.

sentences.zh: 歷司空主簿、清河王友、中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works, Companion to the Prince of Qinghe, and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works, Companion to the Prince of Qinghe, and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 頗銳於榮利，結婚於元叉，超拜左將軍、濟州刺史，尋加平東將軍。

translations.literal: He was rather keen on glory and profit; he married into the family of Yuan Cha and was abruptly promoted to General of the Left and Inspector of Jizhou, soon with the additional title General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: He was keen on glory and profit. He married into Yuan Cha's family and was abruptly promoted to General of the Left and Inspector of Jizhou, soon receiving the additional title General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 清靜愛民，有政治之稱。

translations.literal: He was pure and quiet and loved the people, winning a reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with purity and cared for the people, earning a reputation for good administration.

sentences.zh: 入為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He entered court as Attendant at the Palace Cadet.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as Attendant at the Palace Cadet.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，遷鎮南將軍、金紫光祿大夫，領國子祭酒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaozhuang, he was promoted to General Who Guards the South and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal, and concurrently Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiaozhuang reign he was promoted to General Who Guards the South and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal, and made Director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 永安元年冬卒，年三十七。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Yong'an he died, aged thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the first year of the Yong'an reign he died, at the age of thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、衞將軍、司空公、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Palace Attendant, General of the Guard, Minister of Works, and Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Palace Attendant, General of the Guard, Minister of Works, and Inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 子淵，武定中，儀同開府記室參軍。

translations.literal: His son Yuan, during Wuding, Secretary to the General with Ceremonies Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuan served as Secretary to the General with Ceremonies Equal to the Three Dukes during the Wuding reign.

sentences.zh: 宋弁，字義和，廣平列人人也。

translations.literal: Song Bian, styled Yihe, was a man of Lieren in Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Song Bian, whose courtesy name was Yihe, came from Lieren in Guangping.

sentences.zh: 祖愔，與從叔宣、博陵崔建俱知名。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yin, together with his father's younger cousin Xuan and Cui Jian of Boling, were all renowned.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yin, together with his father's younger cousin Xuan and Cui Jian of Boling, were all well known.

sentences.zh: 世祖時，歷位中書博士、員外散騎常侍，使江南，賜爵列人子，還拜廣平太守。

translations.literal: During Shizu, he successively held the posts of Doctor of the Palace Secretariat and Acting Attendant at the Palace Cadet; he was sent to Jiangnan, granted the title Viscount of Lieren, and on return appointed Administrator of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizu he served as Doctor of the Palace Secretariat and Acting Attendant at the Palace Cadet, was sent on a mission to Jiangnan, and was granted the title Viscount of Lieren. On his return he was appointed Administrator of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 興安五年卒，[4]贈安遠將軍、相州刺史，諡曰惠。

translations.literal: He died in the fifth year of Xing'an;[4] posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the Distant and Inspector of Xiang Province; posthumous title Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of the Xing'an reign.[4] He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the Distant and Inspector of Xiang Province, with the posthumous title Hui.

sentences.zh: 長子顯襲爵。

translations.literal: His eldest son Xian inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Xian inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 弁伯父世顯無子，[5]養弁為後。

translations.literal: Bian's father's elder brother Shixian had no son;[5] he adopted Bian as his heir.
translations.idiomatic: Bian's father's elder brother Shixian had no son[5] and adopted Bian as his heir.

sentences.zh: 弁父叔珍，李敷妹夫，因敷事而死。

translations.literal: Bian's father Shuzhen was the husband of Li Fu's sister and died on account of the Fu affair.
translations.idiomatic: Bian's father Shuzhen was married to Li Fu's sister and was put to death in connection with the Li Fu affair.

sentences.zh: 弁才學儁贍，少有美名。

translations.literal: Bian's talent and learning were outstanding and abundant; from youth he had a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Bian was outstanding in talent and learning and enjoyed a fine reputation from youth.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，曾至京師，見尚書李沖，因言論移日。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Gaozu, he once came to the capital, met the Director of the Imperial Secretariat Li Chong, and their discussion lasted a full day.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Gaozu reign he came to the capital and met Director of the Imperial Secretariat Li Chong. Their discussion lasted a full day.

sentences.zh: 沖竦然異之，退而言曰：「此人一日千里，王佐才也。」

translations.literal: Chong was startled and considered him extraordinary; on retiring he said: 'This man advances a thousand li in a day—he has the talent of a king's assistant.'
translations.idiomatic: Chong was astonished and considered him extraordinary. On retiring he said: 'This man advances a thousand li in a day—he has the talent of a king's assistant.'

sentences.zh: 顯卒，弁襲爵。

translations.literal: When Xian died, Bian inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian died, Bian inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 弁與李彪州里，迭相祗好。

translations.literal: Bian and Li Biao were from the same district and region, and mutually showed respect and friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Bian and Li Biao were from the same district and were close friends who treated each other with mutual respect.

sentences.zh: 彪為祕書丞，弁自中散彪請為著作佐郎，尋除尚書殿中郎中。

translations.literal: When Biao was Secretary of the Palace Library, Bian asked Biao, then a Palace Cadet, to obtain for him the post of Assistant Gentleman of the Academy; soon he was appointed Gentleman of the Palace for Palace Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Biao was Secretary of the Palace Library, Bian asked him, then a Palace Cadet, to secure the post of Assistant Gentleman of the Academy for him. He was soon appointed Gentleman of the Palace for Palace Affairs.

sentences.zh: 高祖曾因朝會之次，歷訪治道，弁年少官微，自下而對，聲姿清亮，進止可觀，高祖稱善者久之。

translations.literal: The Emperor Gaozu once, on the occasion of a court assembly, inquired in turn about the way of governance; Bian was young and his office slight; he answered from below; his voice and bearing were clear and bright, his advance and halt admirable; the Emperor Gaozu praised him at length.
translations.idiomatic: At a court assembly the Emperor Gaozu once inquired about the way of governance. Though young and of low rank, Bian answered from the lower ranks in a clear, bright voice with admirable bearing. The emperor praised him at length.

sentences.zh: 因是大被知遇，賜名為弁，意取弁和獻玉，楚王不知寶之也。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was greatly favored and known; he was granted the name Bian, taking the meaning from Bian He presenting jade—the King of Chu did not know it was a treasure.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he won great favor. He was granted the name Bian, alluding to Bian He presenting jade when the King of Chu did not recognize its worth.

sentences.zh: 遷中書侍郎，兼員外常侍，使於蕭賾。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Palace Attendant and concurrently Acting Regular Attendant, and sent on mission to Xiao Ze.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Palace Attendant and Acting Regular Attendant and sent on a mission to Xiao Ze.

sentences.zh: 賾司徒蕭子良、祕書丞王融等皆稱美之，以為志氣謇烈不逮李彪，而體韻和雅、舉止閑邃過之。

translations.literal: Ze's Minister of Education Xiao Ziliang, Secretary of the Palace Library Wang Rong, and others all praised him, considering that in resolve and spirit, forthrightness and fierceness, he did not match Li Biao, but in bodily grace and harmony, elegance of manner and leisurely depth, he surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ze's Minister of Education Xiao Ziliang, Secretary Wang Rong, and others all praised him, finding that in resolve and boldness he did not match Li Biao, but in grace of manner and refined bearing he surpassed him.

sentences.zh: 轉散騎侍郎，時散騎位在中書之右。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant at the Palace Cadet; at the time the Palace Cadet's rank stood to the right of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Attendant at the Palace Cadet, whose rank at the time stood above that of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 高祖曾論江左事，因問弁曰：「卿比南行，入其隅隩，彼政道云何？

translations.literal: The Emperor Gaozu once discussed affairs south of the Yangtze and therefore asked Bian: 'On your recent journey south, you entered their inner recesses—how is their governance?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor Gaozu once discussed affairs south of the Yangtze and asked Bian: 'On your recent mission south you entered their inner circles—how is their governance?

sentences.zh: 興亡之數可得知不？」

translations.literal: Can the numbers of rise and fall be known?'
translations.idiomatic: Can one discern the signs of their rise or fall?'

sentences.zh: 弁對曰：「蕭氏父子無大功於天下，既以逆取，不能順守。

translations.literal: Bian replied: 'The Xiao father and son have no great merit for the realm; having seized power by rebellion, they cannot preserve it by compliance.
translations.idiomatic: Bian replied: 'The Xiao father and son have won no great merit for the realm. Having seized power by rebellion, they cannot preserve it through proper governance.

sentences.zh: 德政不理，徭役滋劇，內無股肱之助，外有怨叛之民，以臣觀之，必不能貽厥孫謀，保有南海。

translations.literal: Virtuous governance is not ordered; corvée labor grows ever heavier; within they have no helpers as arms and thighs; without they have resentful and rebellious people—in my view they surely cannot bequeath plans to their descendants or long hold the southern sea.
translations.idiomatic: Their virtuous governance is in disorder and corvée labor grows ever heavier. Within they lack loyal ministers; without they face resentful and rebellious subjects. In my view they cannot bequeath lasting plans to their descendants or long hold the south.

sentences.zh: 若物憚其威，身免為幸。」

translations.literal: If creatures fear their might, to escape with one's person is already fortunate.'
translations.idiomatic: If men fear their might, merely to escape with one's life is already fortunate.'

sentences.zh: 後車駕南征，以弁為司徒司馬、曜武將軍、東道副將。

translations.literal: Later, when the imperial carriage campaigned south, Bian was made Major of the Minister of Education, General of Shining Martiality, and Deputy Commander of the Eastern Route.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the emperor campaigned south, Bian was made Major of the Minister of Education, General of Shining Martiality, and Deputy Commander of the Eastern Route.

sentences.zh: 軍人有盜馬靽者，斬而徇之，於是三軍振懼，莫敢犯法。

translations.literal: A soldier stole horse reins; he was beheaded and the act displayed; thereupon the three armies were shaken with fear and none dared break the law.
translations.idiomatic: When a soldier stole horse reins, Bian had him beheaded and displayed the punishment. The entire army was shaken with fear, and none dared break the law.

sentences.zh: 黃門郎崔光薦弁自代，高祖不許，然亦賞光知人。

translations.literal: Gentleman at the Yellow Gate Cui Guang recommended Bian to replace himself; the Emperor Gaozu did not permit it, yet also praised Guang for knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman at the Yellow Gate Cui Guang recommended Bian to succeed him, but the Emperor Gaozu would not allow it, though he praised Guang for recognizing talent.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以弁兼黃門，尋即正，兼司徒左長史。

translations.literal: Before long Bian was made concurrent Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, soon made regular, and concurrently Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Bian was made concurrent Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, soon confirmed in that post, and concurrently Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 時大選內外羣官，並定四海士族，弁專參銓量之任，事多稱旨。

translations.literal: At the time there was a great selection of officials within and without, and the clans of the four seas were also fixed; Bian alone took part in the task of evaluation and measurement, and affairs mostly met the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a great selection of officials was underway and the clans of the realm were being ranked. Bian took charge of evaluation, and his decisions mostly met the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 然好言人之陰短，高門大族意所不便者，弁因毀之；

translations.literal: Yet he loved to speak of people's hidden faults; for great gates and great clans whom he found inconvenient, Bian would therefore slander them;
translations.idiomatic: Yet he loved to speak of people's hidden faults. When great clans displeased him, he would slander them;

sentences.zh: 至於舊族淪滯，人非可忌者，又申達之。

translations.literal: as for old clans fallen into neglect, people who were not to be feared, he would again bring them forward.
translations.idiomatic: but for old clans fallen into neglect, or men who posed no threat, he would bring them forward again.

sentences.zh: 弁又為本州大中正，姓族多所降抑，頗為時人所怨。

translations.literal: Bian was also Chief Rectifier of his native province; many clans and surnames he demoted and suppressed, and he was rather resented by people of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Bian also served as Chief Rectifier of his native province and demoted many clans, earning considerable resentment.

sentences.zh: 從駕南討，詔弁於豫州都督所部及東荊領葉，皆減戍士營農，[6]水陸兼作。

translations.literal: Accompanying the imperial carriage on the southern campaign, an edict ordered Bian that in the areas under the Commander of Yu Province and in Ye under Eastern Jing, garrison soldiers should all be reduced to farm the fields,[6] with work on both water and land.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign an edict ordered Bian to reduce garrison troops under the Commander of Yu Province and in Ye under Eastern Jing and set them to farming,[6] with work on both water and land.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍，尋遷右衞將軍，領黃門。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant at the Palace Cadet, soon promoted to General of the Right Guard, and concurrently head of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant at the Palace Cadet, then soon to General of the Right Guard while retaining headship of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 弁屢自陳讓，高祖曰：「吾為相知者，卿亦不可有辭，豈得專守一官，不助朕為治？

translations.literal: Bian repeatedly memorialized to decline; the Emperor Gaozu said: 'As one who knows and esteems you, you too may not decline—how can you hold to a single office alone and not assist me in governing?
translations.idiomatic: Bian repeatedly asked to decline additional posts. The Emperor Gaozu said: 'As one who knows and esteems you, you may not decline. How can you hold to a single office and not assist me in governing?

sentences.zh: 且常侍者黃門之粗冗，領軍者二衞之假攝，不足空存推讓，以棄大委。」

translations.literal: Moreover, Attendant at the Palace Cadet is a rough and subordinate post of the Yellow Gate; commanding the guard is a provisional assignment of the Two Guards—not enough to preserve empty declinations and abandon great commissions.'
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Attendant at the Palace Cadet is a subordinate post of the Yellow Gate, and commanding the guard is a provisional assignment of the Two Guards—not reason enough to keep declining and abandon great responsibilities.'

sentences.zh: 其被知遇如此。

translations.literal: Thus was he favored and known.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the favor he enjoyed.

sentences.zh: 始，高祖北都之選也，李沖多所參預，頗抑宋氏。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when the Emperor Gaozu selected the northern capital, Li Chong took much part and rather suppressed the Song clan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Emperor Gaozu selected the northern capital, Li Chong took a leading part and rather suppressed the Song clan.

sentences.zh: 弁有恨於沖，而與李彪交結，雅相知重。

translations.literal: Bian bore resentment toward Chong and formed ties with Li Biao, mutually esteeming each other with deep regard.
translations.idiomatic: Bian resented Chong and formed a close alliance with Li Biao, and the two held each other in high regard.

sentences.zh: 及彪之抗沖，沖謂彪曰：「爾如狗耳，為人所嗾。」

translations.literal: When Biao resisted Chong, Chong said to Biao: 'You are like a dog, set on by others.'
translations.idiomatic: When Biao opposed Chong, Chong told him: 'You are no better than a dog set on by others.'

sentences.zh: 及沖劾彪，不至大罪，弁之力也。

translations.literal: When Chong impeached Biao, he did not suffer the greatest penalty—it was through Bian's effort.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong impeached Biao, Biao escaped the severest penalty through Bian's intervention.

sentences.zh: 彪除名為民，弁大相嗟慨，密圖申復。

translations.literal: Biao was struck from the rolls and made a commoner; Bian greatly sighed and lamented, secretly plotting to restore him.
translations.idiomatic: Biao was struck from the rolls and reduced to commoner status. Bian lamented deeply and secretly plotted to restore him.

sentences.zh: 高祖在汝南不豫，大漸，旬有餘日，不見侍臣，左右唯彭城王勰等數人而已。

translations.literal: The Emperor Gaozu was unwell at Runan and grew critically ill; for more than ten days he did not see attending ministers—only the Prince of Pengcheng Xie and a few others were at his side.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor Gaozu fell gravely ill at Runan. For more than ten days he received no attending ministers; only the Prince of Pengcheng Xie and a few others remained at his side.

sentences.zh: 小瘳，乃引見門下及宗室長幼諸人，入者未能知致悲泣，弁獨進及御床，歔欷流涕曰：「臣不謂陛下聖顏毀瘠乃爾！」

translations.literal: When he recovered slightly, he summoned those of the Gate and Below and the elders and juniors of the imperial clan; those who entered, unable to know what to say, wept in grief; Bian alone advanced to the imperial couch, sobbing and shedding tears: 'I did not think Your Majesty's sacred countenance would be so wasted and emaciated!'
translations.idiomatic: When he recovered slightly, he summoned the officials of the Gate and Below and the elders and juniors of the imperial clan. Those who entered wept in grief, unable to find words. Bian alone advanced to the imperial couch, sobbing: 'I never imagined Your Majesty's countenance would be so wasted and emaciated!'

sentences.zh: 由是益重之。

translations.literal: Thereby he was esteemed all the more.
translations.idiomatic: From this he won still greater esteem.

sentences.zh: 車駕征馬圈，留弁以本官兼祠部尚書，攝七兵事。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned at Maquan, Bian was left with his former office and concurrently Director of the Ministry of Sacrifices, overseeing the affairs of the Seven Troops.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned at Maquan, Bian was left in the capital with his former office while also serving as Director of the Ministry of Sacrifices and overseeing the affairs of the Seven Troops.

sentences.zh: 及行，執其手曰：「國之大事，在祀與戎，故令卿綰攝二曹，可不自勉。」

translations.literal: As he departed, he took his hand and said: 'The great affairs of the state lie in sacrifice and war—therefore I have ordered you to hold both ministries together; you must urge yourself on.'
translations.idiomatic: As he departed, he took Bian's hand and said: 'The great affairs of the state lie in sacrifice and war. I have therefore placed both ministries in your hands—you must exert yourself.'

sentences.zh: 弁頓首辭謝。

translations.literal: Bian bowed his head to the ground and declined with thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Bian bowed to the ground and thanked him.

sentences.zh: 弁劬勞王事，夙夜在公，恩遇之甚，輩流莫及，名重朝野，亞於李沖。

translations.literal: Bian toiled at the king's affairs, diligent from dawn to dusk; his favor was very great, his peers could not match him, his name weighed heavy in court and countryside, second only to Li Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Bian toiled tirelessly at state affairs from dawn to dusk. His favor was extraordinary, his peers could not match him, and his reputation in court and countryside was second only to Li Chong.

sentences.zh: 高祖每稱弁可為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: The Emperor Gaozu often said Bian could serve as Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor Gaozu often said that Bian was fit to serve as Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 及崩，遺詔以弁為之，與咸陽王禧等六人輔政，而弁已先卒，年四十八。

translations.literal: When he died, his final edict appointed Bian to that post, with the Prince of Xianyang Xi and five others to assist in government—but Bian had already died first, aged forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: At his death his final edict appointed Bian to that post, with the Prince of Xianyang Xi and five others as regents—but Bian had already died, at the age of forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 詔賜錢十萬、布三百匹，贈安東將軍、瀛州刺史，諡曰貞順。

translations.literal: An edict granted one hundred thousand cash and three hundred bolts of cloth; posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Ying Province; posthumous title Zhenshun.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted one hundred thousand cash and three hundred bolts of cloth. He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Ying Province, with the posthumous title Zhenshun.

sentences.zh: 弁性好矜伐，自許膏腴。

translations.literal: Bian by nature loved to boast and exalt himself, considering himself of the richest stock.
translations.idiomatic: Bian was boastful by nature and considered his clan among the finest.

sentences.zh: 高祖以郭祚晉魏名門，從容謂弁曰：「卿固應推郭祚之門也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor Gaozu, because Guo Zuo was a famous gate of Jin and Wei, said calmly to Bian: 'You surely ought to defer to Guo Zuo's house.'
translations.idiomatic: Because Guo Zuo came from a famous Jin and Wei clan, the Emperor Gaozu said calmly to Bian: 'You surely ought to defer to Guo Zuo's house.'

sentences.zh: 弁笑曰：「臣家未肯推祚。」

translations.literal: Bian laughed and said: 'My house is not willing to defer to Zuo.'
translations.idiomatic: Bian laughed and said: 'My house is not willing to defer to him.'

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「卿自漢魏以來，既無高官，又無儁秀，何得不推？」

translations.literal: The Emperor Gaozu said: 'Your house since Han and Wei has had neither high offices nor outstanding talents—how can you fail to defer?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: 'Since Han and Wei your house has produced neither high offices nor outstanding talents—how can you refuse to defer?'

sentences.zh: 弁曰：「臣清素自立，要爾不推。」

translations.literal: Bian said: 'I stand on purity and simplicity—I simply will not defer.'
translations.idiomatic: Bian said: 'I stand on my own integrity—I simply will not defer.'
