sentences.zh: 侍臣出後，高祖謂彭城王勰曰：「弁人身良自不惡，乃復欲以門戶自矜，殊為可怪。」

translations.literal: After the attending ministers had left, the Emperor Gaozu said to the Prince of Pengcheng Xie: 'Bian's person in itself is not bad, yet he still wishes to pride himself on his gate and house—this is quite strange.'
translations.idiomatic: After the ministers had left, the emperor said to the Prince of Pengcheng Xie: 'Bian is not a bad man in himself, yet he still prides himself on his clan—how strange.'

sentences.zh: 長子維，字伯緒。

translations.literal: His eldest son Wei, styled Boxu.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Wei, whose courtesy name was Boxu.

sentences.zh: 維弟紀，字仲烈。

translations.literal: Wei's younger brother Ji, styled Zhonglie.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's younger brother Ji, whose courtesy name was Zhonglie.

sentences.zh: 維少襲父爵，自員外郎遷給事中。

translations.literal: Wei in youth inherited his father's title; from Gentleman of the Palace he was promoted to Attendant at the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Wei inherited his father's title in youth and rose from Gentleman of the Palace to Attendant at the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 坐諂事高肇，出為益州龍驤府長史，辭疾不行。

translations.literal: For toadying to Gao Zhao, he was sent out as Chief Clerk of the Dragon-Agile Commandery in Yi Province, but pleaded illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: For currying favor with Gao Zhao, he was sent out as Chief Clerk of the Dragon-Agile Commandery in Yi Province, but pleaded illness and refused to go.

sentences.zh: 太尉、清河王懌輔政，以維名臣之子，薦為通直郎，辟其弟紀行參軍。

translations.literal: The Grand Minister, the Prince of Qinghe Yi, assisted in government; because Wei was the son of a famous minister, he recommended him as Direct Attendant and appointed his younger brother Ji as Acting Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Minister, the Prince of Qinghe Yi, took charge of government, he recommended Wei as Direct Attendant because he was the son of a famous minister, and appointed his younger brother Ji as Acting Staff Officer.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨政，委任元叉，而叉恃寵驕盈，懌每以分理裁斷。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling held the government; she entrusted Yuan Cha, but Cha relied on favor and was arrogant and excessive; Yi often judged cases with impartial reason.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling held power she entrusted Yuan Cha, but Cha grew arrogant on imperial favor while Yi often judged cases with impartial reason.

sentences.zh: 叉甚忿恨，思以害懌，遂與維為計，以富貴許之。

translations.literal: Cha was deeply resentful and thought to harm Yi; he then plotted with Wei and promised him wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: Cha resented this deeply and plotted to destroy Yi. He conspired with Wei and promised him wealth and honor.

sentences.zh: 維見叉寵勢日隆，便至乾沒，乃告司染都尉韓文殊父子欲謀逆立懌。

translations.literal: Wei saw Cha's favor and power growing daily and went so far as outright seizure; he reported that the Commandant of the Dye Office Han Wenshu and his son plotted rebellion to install Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Cha's power grow daily, Wei went to outrageous lengths and reported that Commandant of the Dye Office Han Wenshu and his son were plotting rebellion to install Yi on the throne.

sentences.zh: 懌坐被錄禁中。

translations.literal: Yi on that account was arrested and confined within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On this charge Yi was arrested and confined within the palace.

sentences.zh: 文殊父子懼而逃遁。

translations.literal: Wenshu and his son, in fear, fled and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu and his son fled in fear.

sentences.zh: 鞫無反狀。

translations.literal: Under interrogation there was no sign of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Interrogation found no evidence of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 以文殊亡走，懸處大辟。

translations.literal: Because Wenshu had fled, he was sentenced in absentia to execution.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wenshu had fled, he was sentenced in absentia to death.

sentences.zh: 置懌於宮西別館，禁兵守之。

translations.literal: Yi was placed in a separate lodge west of the palace, guarded by forbidden troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was placed in a separate lodge west of the palace and guarded by imperial troops.

sentences.zh: 維應反坐，叉言於太后，欲開將來告者之路，乃黜為燕州昌平郡守，紀為秦州大羌令。

translations.literal: Wei should have been punished by the law of retaliation; Cha spoke to the Empress Dowager, wishing to open the path for future informers, and had him demoted to Administrator of Changping in Yan Province, and Ji made Magistrate of Daqiang in Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Wei should have been punished by law, but Cha told the Empress Dowager he wished to encourage future informers. Wei was demoted to Administrator of Changping in Yan Province, and Ji was made Magistrate of Daqiang in Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 維及紀頗涉經史，而浮薄無行。

translations.literal: Wei and Ji had read considerably in the classics and histories, but were frivolous and without conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Ji had read widely in the classics and histories, but were frivolous and unprincipled.

sentences.zh: 懌親尊懿望，朝野瞻屬，維受懌眷賞，而無狀構間，天下人士莫不怪忿而賤薄之。

translations.literal: Yi was a kinsman of honored standing and fine reputation, looked to by court and countryside; Wei had received Yi's affection and rewards, yet without cause fabricated estrangement—all men under heaven none failed to marvel in anger and despise him lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was a kinsman of honored standing whom court and countryside alike looked to with respect. Wei had enjoyed Yi's affection and rewards, yet without cause fabricated a conspiracy against him. Men throughout the realm marveled in anger and despised him.

sentences.zh: 及叉殺懌，專斷朝政，以維兄弟前者告懌，徵維為散騎侍郎，紀為太學博士，領侍御史，甚昵之。

translations.literal: When Cha killed Yi and monopolized court government, because the Wei brothers had earlier informed on Yi, Wei was summoned as Attendant at the Palace Cadet and Ji as Doctor of the Imperial Academy, concurrently Attending Censor; he was very intimate with them.
translations.idiomatic: When Cha killed Yi and monopolized the government, he recalled the Wei brothers for having informed on Yi. Wei was made Attendant at the Palace Cadet and Ji Doctor of the Imperial Academy and Attending Censor, and Cha treated them with great intimacy.

sentences.zh: 維超遷通直常侍，又除冠軍將軍、洛州刺史；

translations.literal: Wei was abruptly promoted to Direct Regular Attendant, and also appointed General Who Wins the Championship and Inspector of Luo Province;
translations.idiomatic: Wei was abruptly promoted to Direct Regular Attendant and also made General Who Wins the Championship and Inspector of Luo Province;

sentences.zh: 紀超遷尚書郎。

translations.literal: Ji was abruptly promoted to Gentleman of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was abruptly promoted to Gentleman of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，弁謂族弟世景言：「維性疏險，而紀識慧不足，終必敗吾業也。」

translations.literal: Earlier Bian had said to his clansman younger brother Shijing: 'Wei's nature is careless and dangerous, while Ji's insight and wisdom are insufficient—they will in the end ruin my legacy.'
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Bian had told his clansman Shijing: 'Wei is reckless and dangerous, and Ji's insight is insufficient—they will ruin my legacy in the end.'

sentences.zh: 世景以為不爾，至是果然，聞者以為知子莫若父。

translations.literal: Shijing thought it would not be so, but when the time came it was indeed so; those who heard said that none knows a son like the father.
translations.idiomatic: Shijing thought otherwise, but events proved Bian right. Those who heard said that no one knows a son like his father.

sentences.zh: 尚書令李崇、尚書左僕射郭祚、右僕射游肇每云：「伯緒兇疏，終敗宋氏，幸得殺身耳。」

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Secretariat Li Chong, Left Vice Director Guo Zuo, and Right Vice Director You Zhao often said: 'Boxu is vicious and careless; he will in the end ruin the Song clan—fortunate if he dies by the sword.'
translations.idiomatic: Director Li Chong, Left Vice Director Guo Zuo, and Right Vice Director You Zhao often said: 'Boxu is vicious and reckless and will ruin the Song clan in the end—fortunate if he dies by the sword.'

sentences.zh: 論者以為有徵。

translations.literal: Commentators considered this prophetic.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators considered this prophetic.

sentences.zh: 後除營州刺史，仍本將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Inspector of Ying Province, retaining his former general's title.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Inspector of Ying Province while retaining his former general's title.

sentences.zh: 靈太后反政，以叉黨除名，遂還鄉里。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling restored the government, as a member of Cha's faction he was struck from the rolls and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling restored the government, he was struck from the rolls as a member of Cha's faction and returned to his home district.

sentences.zh: 尋追其前誣告清河王事，於鄴賜死。

translations.literal: Soon his earlier false accusation against the Prince of Qinghe was pursued, and he was granted death at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his earlier false accusation against the Prince of Qinghe was pursued, and he was ordered to take his own life at Ye.

sentences.zh: 子春卿，早亡。

translations.literal: His son Chunqing died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chunqing died young.

sentences.zh: 弟紀以次子欽仁繼。

translations.literal: His younger brother Ji had his second son Qinren succeed.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Ji had his second son Qinren succeed to the line.

sentences.zh: 欽仁，武定末，太尉祭酒。

translations.literal: Qinren, at the end of Wuding, Libationer to the Grand Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Qinren served as Libationer to the Grand Minister at the end of the Wuding reign.

sentences.zh: 紀，肅宗末，為北道行臺。

translations.literal: Ji, at the end of Suzong, was Northern Route Mobile Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Suzong reign Ji served as Northern Route Mobile Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 卒於晉陽。

translations.literal: He died at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 子欽道，武定末，冀州別駕。

translations.literal: His son Qindao, at the end of Wuding, Vice Director of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qindao served as Vice Director of Ji Province at the end of the Wuding reign.

sentences.zh: 弁弟機，本州治中。

translations.literal: Bian's younger brother Ji was Administrator of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: Bian's younger brother Ji served as Administrator of his native province.

sentences.zh: 子寶積，卒於中散大夫。

translations.literal: His son Baoji died while holding the post of Grand Master of Leisure.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baoji died while serving as Grand Master of Leisure.

sentences.zh: 弁族弟穎，字文賢。

translations.literal: Bian's clansman younger brother Ying, styled Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: Bian's clansman Ying, whose courtesy name was Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 自奉朝請稍遷尚書郎、魏郡太守。

translations.literal: From Court Attendant he was gradually promoted to Gentleman of the Imperial Secretariat and Administrator of Wei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from Court Attendant to Gentleman of the Imperial Secretariat and Administrator of Wei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 納貨劉騰，騰言之於元叉，以穎為冠軍將軍、涼州刺史。

translations.literal: He gave bribes to Liu Teng; Teng spoke of him to Yuan Cha, and Ying was made General Who Wins the Championship and Inspector of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He bribed Liu Teng, who spoke of him to Yuan Cha. Ying was then made General Who Wins the Championship and Inspector of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 穎前妻鄧氏亡後十五年，穎夢見之，向穎拜曰：「新婦今被處分為高崇妻，故來辭君。」

translations.literal: Fifteen years after Ying's former wife Lady Deng died, Ying dreamed he saw her; she bowed to Ying and said: 'Your new wife has now been assigned to be the wife of Gao Chong—therefore I come to take leave of you.'
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen years after Ying's former wife Lady Deng died, Ying dreamed of her. She bowed to him and said: 'Your new wife has now been assigned to become Gao Chong's wife, and I have come to take leave of you.'

sentences.zh: 泫然流涕。

translations.literal: Tears streamed down her face.
translations.idiomatic: Tears streamed down her face.

sentences.zh: 穎旦而見崇言之，崇後數日而卒。

translations.literal: At dawn Ying saw Chong and told him; Chong died a few days later.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Ying told Chong what he had dreamed, and Chong died a few days later.

sentences.zh: 穎族弟燮，字崇和。

translations.literal: Ying's clansman younger brother Xie, styled Chonghe.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's clansman Xie, whose courtesy name was Chonghe.

sentences.zh: 廣平王懷郎中令、員外常侍。

translations.literal: Director of the Household of the Prince of Guangping Huai and Acting Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Director of the Household of the Prince of Guangping Huai and Acting Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 為征北李平司馬，北殄元愉，頗有贊謀之功。

translations.literal: As Major to Li Ping, General Who Conquers the North, he exterminated Yuan Yu in the north and had considerable merit in planning and counsel.
translations.idiomatic: As Major to Li Ping, General Who Conquers the North, he helped destroy Yuan Yu in the north and contributed significantly to planning and counsel.

sentences.zh: 燮族弟鴻貴，為定州平北府參軍，送兵於荊州。

translations.literal: Xie's clansman younger brother Honggui was a Staff Officer of the Pacify-the-North Commandery in Ding Province, escorting troops to Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Xie's clansman Honggui was a Staff Officer of the Pacify-the-North Commandery in Ding Province, escorting troops to Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 坐取兵絹四百匹，兵欲告之，乃斬十人。

translations.literal: For seizing four hundred bolts of soldiers' silk, when the soldiers wished to report him, he beheaded ten men.
translations.idiomatic: He seized four hundred bolts of soldiers' silk. When the soldiers threatened to report him, he beheaded ten of them.

sentences.zh: 又疏凡不達律令，見律有梟首之罪，乃生斷兵手，以水澆之，然後斬決。

translations.literal: Moreover he was crude and ignorant of the laws and ordinances; seeing that the law had the crime of exposing the head on display, he cut off a soldier's hand while alive, poured water on it, and then beheaded and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: He was crude and ignorant of the law. Seeing that the statutes provided for the crime of exposing the head on display, he cut off a soldier's hand while the man was still alive, poured water on it, and then beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 尋坐伏法。

translations.literal: Soon he was punished by execution.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon executed.

sentences.zh: 時人哀兵之苦，笑鴻貴之愚。

translations.literal: People of the time pitied the soldiers' suffering and laughed at Honggui's folly.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time pitied the soldiers' suffering and laughed at Honggui's folly.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：古人有云，才未半古，功以過之，非徒語也。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The ancients had a saying that when one's talent is not half that of antiquity, one's achievements may surpass it—this is no empty phrase.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer remarks: The ancients said that when one's talent falls short of antiquity, one's achievements may still surpass it—this is no empty saying.

sentences.zh: 王肅流寓之人，見知一面，雖器業自致，抑亦逢時，榮任赫然，寄同舊列，美矣。

translations.literal: Wang Su was a man who had wandered and sojourned abroad; he was known through a single meeting; though his capacity and achievement came through his own effort, he also met the right time; his honored appointments blazed forth, ranking with the old ministers—beautiful indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su was a sojourner from abroad who won recognition in a single audience. Though his achievements were his own, he also met the right moment. His honors blazed forth and placed him among the old ministers—admirable indeed.

sentences.zh: 誦翊繼軌，不殞光風。

translations.literal: Song and Yi followed in his track and did not let his luminous wind perish.
translations.idiomatic: Song and Yi followed in his footsteps and did not let his luminous reputation fade.

sentences.zh: 宋弁以才度見知，迹參顧命，拔萃出類，其有以哉。

translations.literal: Song Bian was known through talent and measure; his traces joined in the entrusted mandate; he stood out from the crowd and surpassed his class—there was reason for it.
translations.idiomatic: Song Bian was recognized for his talent and capacity and took part in the entrusted regency. He stood out from the crowd—there was good reason for it.

sentences.zh: 無子之歎，豈徒羊舌，宗祀之不亡，幸矣。

translations.literal: The sigh over having no son—is it only Yangshe? That the ancestral sacrifices did not perish was fortunate indeed.
translations.idiomatic: The lament over having no son was not Yangshe's alone. That the ancestral sacrifices did not perish was fortunate indeed.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation Notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 除持節都督豫東豫東郢三州諸軍事 諸本「東豫」二字缺，今據冊府卷三八一

translations.literal: Appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in the three provinces of Eastern Yu, Eastern Yu, and Ying: In various editions the two characters 'Eastern Yu' are missing; now supplemented according to Cefu, juan 381
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in the three provinces of Eastern Yu, Eastern Yu, and Ying: Various editions lack the two characters 'Eastern Yu'; the text is here restored from Cefu, juan 381

sentences.zh: 〈四五三三頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 4533〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈page 4533〉

sentences.zh: 補。

translations.literal: supplemented.
translations.idiomatic: supplemented.

sentences.zh: 又冊府「東郢」無「東」字，檢一０六中地形志中北揚州汝陰郡條稱「太和十八年為東郢州，後罷」，又文館詞林卷六六二後魏孝文帝出師詔，亦見「東郢州」。

translations.literal: Moreover in Cefu 'Eastern Ying' lacks the character 'east'; checking the Treatise on Geography in 106, the entry for Ruyin in Northern Yangzhou states 'In the eighteenth year of Taihe it became Eastern Ying Province, later abolished'; also in Wen'guan Cilin, juan 662, the Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen's campaign edict likewise has 'Eastern Ying Province.'
translations.idiomatic: Cefu also lacks the character 'east' in 'Eastern Ying.' The Treatise on Geography (106), entry for Ruyin in Northern Yangzhou, states that in the eighteenth year of Taihe it became Eastern Ying Province and was later abolished. Wen'guan Cilin, juan 662, likewise records 'Eastern Ying Province' in Emperor Xiaowen's campaign edict.

sentences.zh: 知有「東」字不誤。

translations.literal: Thus one knows the character 'east' is not in error.
translations.idiomatic: This confirms that the character 'east' is correct.

sentences.zh: 從叔廣陽宗室尊宿 諸本及北史卷四二王肅傳「陽」作「陵」。

translations.literal: Father's younger cousin, the Prince of Guangyang, senior of the imperial clan: In various editions and in Beishi, juan 42, Wang Su's biography, 'yang' is written as 'ling.'
translations.idiomatic: Father's younger cousin, the Prince of Guangyang, senior of the imperial clan: Various editions and Beishi, juan 42, Wang Su's biography, read 'yang' as 'ling.'

sentences.zh: 按當時無所謂「宗室尊宿」封於廣陵。

translations.literal: According to investigation, at the time there was no so-called 'senior of the imperial clan' enfeoffed at Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was no senior member of the imperial clan enfeoffed at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 據卷七下高祖紀下太和二十三年二月稱以王肅為尚書令，廣陽王嘉為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: According to Juan 7b, Gaozu's Annals, second month of the twenty-third year of Taihe, Wang Su was made Director of the Imperial Secretariat and the Prince of Guangyang Jia was made Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Juan 7b of Gaozu's Annals records that in the second month of the twenty-third year of Taihe, Wang Su was made Director of the Imperial Secretariat and the Prince of Guangyang Jia Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 故元澄說王肅不應位居嘉之上，嘉為拓跋燾孫，澄為燾曾孫，故稱嘉為「從叔」。

translations.literal: Therefore Yuan Cheng said Wang Su should not stand above Jia; Jia was the grandson of Tuoba Tao, Cheng was Tao's great-grandson—hence Jia was called 'father's younger cousin.'
translations.idiomatic: Hence Yuan Cheng objected that Wang Su should not rank above Jia. Jia was the grandson of Tuoba Tao and Cheng his great-grandson, which is why Jia was called 'father's younger cousin.'

sentences.zh: 「廣陵」顯為「廣陽」之訛，今改正。

translations.literal: 'Guangling' is clearly an error for 'Guangyang'—now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: 'Guangling' is clearly an error for 'Guangyang' and is corrected here.

sentences.zh: 興安五年卒 張森楷云：「興安只二年，『五』當是『二』之訛。」

translations.literal: Died in the fifth year of Xing'an: Zhang Senkai says: 'Xing'an had only two years; "five" must be an error for "two."'
translations.idiomatic: Died in the fifth year of Xing'an: Zhang Senkai notes: 'The Xing'an reign had only two years; "five" must be an error for "two."'

sentences.zh: 長子顯襲爵弁伯父世顯無子 張森楷云：「弁伯父即愔長子，而上云『顯』，下云『世顯』。

translations.literal: The eldest son Xian inherited the title; Bian's father's elder brother Shixian had no son: Zhang Senkai says: 'Bian's father's elder brother is Yin's eldest son, yet above it says "Xian" and below "Shixian."
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Xian inherited the title; Bian's father's elder brother Shixian had no son: Zhang Senkai notes: 'Bian's father's elder brother was Yin's eldest son, yet above the text reads "Xian" and below "Shixian."

sentences.zh: 據下云：『顯卒，弁襲爵。』

translations.literal: According to what follows: "When Xian died, Bian inherited the title."
translations.idiomatic: The text below states: 'When Xian died, Bian inherited the title.'

sentences.zh: 北史

translations.literal: Beishi
translations.idiomatic: Beishi

sentences.zh: 〈卷二六〉

translations.literal: 〈juan 26〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈juan 26〉

sentences.zh: 亦無『顯』字，疑『世』字不當有。」

translations.literal: also lacks the character 'Xian'; it is suspected the character 'shi' should not be present.'
translations.idiomatic: also lacks the character for Xian; the character 'shi' is probably spurious.'

sentences.zh: 按「弁伯父」三字也是贅文，疑是後人旁注羼入。

translations.literal: According to investigation, the three characters 'Bian's father's elder brother' are also superfluous text, suspected to be a later marginal note worked into the main text.
translations.idiomatic: The three characters 'Bian's father's elder brother' are also probably superfluous, likely a later marginal note worked into the main text.

sentences.zh: 詔弁於豫州都督所部及東荊領葉皆減戍士營農 冊府卷五０三

translations.literal: Edict ordering Bian that in the areas under the Commander of Yu Province and in Ye under Eastern Jing, garrison soldiers should all be reduced to farm the fields: Cefu, juan 503
translations.idiomatic: Edict ordering Bian to reduce garrison troops under the Commander of Yu Province and in Ye under Eastern Jing and set them to farming: Cefu, juan 503

sentences.zh: 〈六０三五頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 6035〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈page 6035〉

sentences.zh: 「領葉」作「潁鄴」。

translations.literal: 'Command Ye' is written as 'Ying and Ye.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Command Ye' is written as 'Ying and Ye.'

sentences.zh: 按「領葉」不可解，「領」或是「潁」之訛，然鄴太遠，也可疑。

translations.literal: According to investigation, 'Command Ye' cannot be explained; 'command' may be an error for 'Ying,' yet Ye is too far away and is also doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: 'Command Ye' is unintelligible; 'command' may be an error for 'Ying,' though Ye is geographically distant and also doubtful.
